clue.text: Prepare to fire, holding line before fortress — will it hold up the enemy's progress?

definitions.text: will it hold up the enemy's progress?

indicators.note: the first assembled piece comes before the fortress word in the answer
the gun-readying word keeps the line abbreviation held within it

parts.note: to cock a gun is to make it ready to fire
a tower is a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: A gunner readies a weapon by a castle wall, wondering whether the defences will slow an invading army.
explanation.walkthrough: The enemy here is time (as in 'time is the enemy'); a tower with a clock on it holds up the clock, and so, playfully, holds up time's progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Its face displays the hours, so the building carries aloft the passing of time, the proverbial enemy.

clue.text: Architect left city, otherwise given more employment

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London
or introduces an alternative, meaning otherwise
someone given more work is busier

explanation.surface: An architect quits town or, put another way, finds himself taking on extra work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss-French modernist designer of the Villa Savoye is perhaps the most famous architect of the twentieth century.

clue.text: With cold' meat, attendant brought round new wine

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ham is a cured meat

indicators.note: the servant word is put around the abbreviation for new

parts.note: a page is a boy attendant

explanation.surface: Cold cuts are served and a waiter carries round a fresh bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparkling drink from the French region is a famous kind of wine.

clue.text: One with three lines of equipment to fit into vehicle

indicators.note: the gear word is placed inside the transport word

parts.note: a tram is a street vehicle running on rails
a rig is a set of equipment, as for drilling

explanation.surface: Someone loads three rows of gear into a van.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a figure made of three lines, such as the hexagram-halves of the I Ching.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix tri- means three and -gram a written figure, so it is a symbol built from three strokes.

clue.text: One of two blades sweeping though the water

definitions.text: One of two blades sweeping though the water

parts.words: One of two blades sweeping though the water
parts.note: reads like an oar of a rowing pair, but describes a car part whose rubber blade sweeps rain off the glass

explanation.surface: A pair of oars pulls through the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Blades and water suggest rowing; the blades are rubber ones on a car, and the water is rain on the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Cars commonly have a pair of these arms whose blades clear rain from the front glass.

clue.text: Income, or people demanding a cut?

definitions.meaning: income, especially that of a government or business
the tax authority, which demands its share of everyone's earnings

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a state's income and, with 'the', the tax office that collects its share.

clue.text: Fancy being seen with that chap!

parts.note: him refers to a man already mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the idea of being spotted in a certain man's company.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing fancy is a sudden impulsive notion or desire.

clue.text: Greeting almost half forgotten by October 31st

indicators.note: nearly half the letters of the festival name, the last four of nine, are dropped

parts.note: the last day of October is the festival of Hallowe'en

explanation.surface: A hello half-remembered on the last night of October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost half forgotten' drops WEEN, four of the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variant spelling of hello, a word of greeting.

clue.text: Just keeping time, in rhythm

indicators.note: the word for simply holds the time letter within it

parts.note: mere means just, as in 'a mere child'

explanation.surface: A musician barely keeps the beat.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse and music the term denotes the regular beat pattern, i.e. the rhythm.

clue.text: Philosopher William's finally abandoned error, holding nothing to be chance

indicators.note: the philosopher's name loses its closing letter

parts.note: William of Occam (Ockham) was the medieval philosopher of Occam's razor

indicators.note: the wrongdoing word keeps the zero letter within it

parts.note: a sin is a moral error
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A student of medieval thought gives up on a mistake and decides it was all down to luck.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunity or favourable moment, as in 'rise to the occasion', is a chance.

clue.text: Name dropped by passionate girl

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name is taken out of the next word

parts.note: violent can mean intensely passionate, as in violent love

explanation.surface: An ardent young woman lets slip someone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's given name, from the flower.

clue.text: Set of pearls brought in by pair for fitting

indicators.note: the necklace word is placed inside the abbreviation for pair

parts.note: a rope is a long string of pearls

explanation.surface: Two people arrive with a pearl necklace for a jeweller's fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and fitting are synonyms meaning appropriate or suitable.

clue.text: Pattern of behaviour said to have been wicked by religious authority

indicators.note: the word for having done wrong is spoken, giving the sound of the first syllable

parts.note: to have been wicked is to have sinned
Rome, seat of the Pope, stands for the authority of the Catholic church

explanation.surface: Someone's habits are denounced as sinful by the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic set of symptoms or behaviours occurring together is a syndrome.

clue.text: Curse that wouldn't pass a lady's lips

definitions.text: Curse that wouldn't pass a lady's lips

parts.words: Curse that wouldn't pass a lady's lips
parts.note: an oath, but also read in two parts: speech belonging to men, which a lady would not utter

explanation.surface: A genteel woman would never utter such a swear word.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as MALE DICTION: men's way of speaking, which by old-fashioned convention a lady would not use.
explanation.definitionFit: A malediction is a spoken curse, the opposite of a benediction or blessing.

clue.text: Called for support in climb

definitions.meaning: a crosspiece of a ladder that you step on while climbing

explanation.definitionFit: It is the past participle of ring, meaning telephoned, and a step on a ladder.

clue.text: Ready to go to shops, but take the wrong way in alley

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the glass-ball word

parts.note: an alley (or alley taw) is a playing marble

indicators.note: the letters of take are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Goods are ready for the shops, but someone heads the wrong way down a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: Alley here is the children's glass marble (an alley taw), not a back lane, and 'the wrong way' is an anagram signal rather than a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something saleable is fit to be sold in the market.

clue.text: Levy cut in shock judgment

indicators.note: the shortened tax word sits inside the horrify word

parts.note: to appal is to shock

indicators.note: the tax word loses its last letter

parts.note: to raise a tax is to levy it

explanation.surface: A tax reduction comes as a shock verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Levy' is a verb here: to raise a tax is to levy it, and 'cut' docks the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an assessment or evaluation, a considered judgment.

clue.text: Man who shot 'Potemkin extremely sure to have plugged a genius

indicators.note: the first and last letters of sure are stuffed into the genius word

parts.note: Albert Einstein is the byword for a genius

indicators.note: only the outermost letters of sure are used

explanation.surface: A gunman in the battleship story is surely held up by a brilliant mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' means filmed: Sergei Eisenstein directed the 1925 film Battleship Potemkin. The first and last letters of 'sure' are S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet director filmed the silent classic Battleship Potemkin, so he is the man who shot it.

clue.text: Grain, as distilled into alcoholic drink

indicators.note: distilling processes the raw material, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Grain is processed in a still to make liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and sometimes brandy.

clue.text: Such clothing unlikely to be magnetic attraction?

definitions.text: Such clothing unlikely to be magnetic attraction?

parts.words: Such clothing unlikely to be magnetic attraction?
parts.note: describes clothes needing no pressing, but also read literally as not containing the metal a magnet attracts

explanation.surface: Wondering whether certain garments could ever be alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothes needing no ironing are, read literally, made of no iron, so a magnet would not attract them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabrics that dry smooth and need no pressing are labelled this way.

clue.text: First of polite notices for sportsman's protection

indicators.note: only the opening letter of polite is used

parts.note: ads are advertisements, public notices

explanation.surface: Courteous advertisements for protective sports gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers and hockey goalkeepers wear these padded guards on their legs.

clue.text: Just made beer with northern ingredients

indicators.note: the conjunction and the northern letter go into the beer word, as ingredients go into a brew

parts.note: a brew is a beer
and means with, joining things

explanation.surface: A freshly made ale uses ingredients from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brand-new is completely new, only just made.

clue.text: Sand here perhaps induced ecstasy in composer

indicators.note: to induce is literally to lead in, so the drug letter goes inside the composer

parts.note: J. S. Bach is the German composer
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug sent a composer into raptures among the sand dunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand is typically found on a shore by the sea, so 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Port invaded by regiment originally in forest

indicators.note: the opening letter of regiment breaks into the port name

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

indicators.note: only the first letter of regiment is taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers originally stationed in woodland invade a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Arden is in Warwickshire, the setting of Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: The English woodland famous from Shakespeare's As You Like It is the Forest of Arden.

clue.text: Meaning to take sister round a church

indicators.note: the sister word goes around the single letter

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone means to escort a nun to a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle shade of meaning is a nuance.

clue.text: Passion is not so simple, as Cockneys might say

indicators.note: London Cockneys drop initial aitches, so the word is said without its first sound

parts.note: harder means less simple, more difficult

explanation.surface: Someone remarks in a London accent that love is more complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class Londoners famous for dropping their H's, so 'harder' becomes 'arder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense enthusiasm or passion.

clue.text: Left one in miserable African town

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: the numeral letter sits inside the unhappy word

parts.note: sad means miserable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller left alone in a gloomy African settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian city at the northern end of the Suez Canal is an African port town.

clue.text: Suggest 'Japanese religion is extremely deficient

indicators.note: the religion's name lacks its first and last letters

parts.note: Shinto is the native religion of Japan

explanation.surface: Someone implies that a Japanese faith falls badly short.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint is to suggest something indirectly.

clue.text: A boring type rejected a dose of cocaine as stimulant

indicators.note: the dull-person word is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: a nerd is a dull, boring person
a line is a measure of powdered cocaine to be snorted

explanation.surface: A dull person turns down cocaine as a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone released in fear or excitement acts as the body's natural stimulant.
